userStories.title: Incremental Graph Diff — Replace Full Re-Import
acceptanceCriteria: IncrementalGraphDiffService.diffAndApply() computes a diff and applies only the delta
Stored graph is loaded from GraphNode + GraphLink Prisma tables; not from LanceDB
When newNodes has 100 nodes and stored has 90, added=10, removed=0
When a stored node is absent from newNodes, it is deleted from both GraphNode table and LanceDB (by graphify nodeId / RAG sourceId)
When a node exists in both with unchanged content, it is skipped (no re-index)
diffAndApply is called by the existing importGraphify endpoint (replaces the current deleteAllBySourceType logic)
DiffResult.indexed reflects only the number of nodes actually written to LanceDB (not the total)
A diff-and-apply of 500 unchanged nodes + 10 added + 5 removed completes in under 2 seconds
DiffResult includes durationMs for performance monitoring
The importGraphify route is gated with @RequiredPermission([KodaAction.IMPORT, 'CodeIntel']); non-permitted callers receive 403 from PermissionAuthGuard
suggestedCriteria: KodaDomainWriter importGraphify metadata remains backward-compatible by mapping DiffResult to imported/cleared fields
When newNodes is empty and stored graph has nodes, all stored nodes are removed from GraphNode and LanceDB
If LanceDB delete/upsert fails for a node, the failure is surfaced in result/logs and does not silently report success
Diff compares normalized node content (including outgoing links) deterministically so link-order differences alone do not cause false updates
A reconciliation path exists to detect and clean orphaned LanceDB code documents not present in GraphNode

userStories.title: AST/Symbol Index Pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: AstIndexService.indexCommit() parses source files and stores symbol metadata in the Symbol Prisma table
Symbol.symbolId uses the convention {repoId}:{filePath}::{SymbolName} and is globally unique within a project
getCallers(symbolId) returns all symbols that include this symbol in their JSON callers list
getCallees(symbolId) returns all symbols in this symbol's JSON callees list
When indexCommit is called with files=[{path: 'src/auth.ts', content: '...'}], only src/auth.ts is parsed (incremental)
Symbol.signature captures parameter types and return type (e.g. (userId: string): Promise<User>)
Indexing is triggered by a code_commit outbox event (fired by VCS webhook handler)
A commit with 20 files (avg 200 lines each) is indexed in under 30 seconds
Direct calls to AstIndexService.indexCommit() are gated with @RequiredPermission([KodaAction.MANAGE, 'AstIndex']); grants to ADMIN users and DEVELOPER agents only
Parser failures for one file are recorded in the result and do not prevent other files in the same commit from being indexed
The code_commit handler resolves changed file contents before calling indexCommit(); the webhook controller only enqueues commit metadata
suggestedCriteria: For each indexed file, prior symbols for that same project/repo/file are atomically replaced to avoid stale duplicates
indexCommit with empty files returns symbolsIndexed=0 and filesIndexed=0 without error
Static import resolution limitations (dynamic imports/external unresolved symbols) are explicitly captured as partial-callgraph behavior
Non-parseable or unsupported files are reported in fileErrors and do not fail the entire commit indexing run
Symbol callers/callees JSON is validated on read/write to prevent malformed persistence

userStories.title: Ticket/Entity Graph Builder
acceptanceCriteria: EntityGraphService.rebuildGraph(projectId) rebuilds all entity nodes and links for a project
Entity graph data is persisted in EntityNode and EntityLink tables, not only in Phase 2's in-memory EntityStore
onTicketEvent(status_changed) updates the entity node for that ticket (if it exists)
onGraphifyImport() extracts service entities from graphify nodes with type=code_module
Initial implementation does not require a Ticket.serviceId column; service linkage works from current Koda fields (gitRefFile, labels, etc.)
getRelatedEntities(projectId, entityId, depth=2) returns all entities reachable within 2 hops
getIncidentImpact(projectId, incidentTicketId) returns all entities linked to the incident
Service entities extracted from graphify inherit tags from the graphify node (e.g. ['backend', 'auth'])
Entity graph is updated incrementally via outbox fan-out (no full rebuild on every event)
A graph with 500 nodes and 2000 edges returns getRelatedEntities in under 50ms
suggestedCriteria: Inference-generated entity links carry confidence/source metadata and manual links are preserved as higher-authority overrides
Graph traversal handles cycles safely and never loops infinitely
Unknown entityId in getRelatedEntities returns a deterministic empty result or typed not-found error
onTicketEvent ignores unsupported event actions without throwing
rebuildGraph clears stale entity links for the target project before rebuilding

userStories.title: VCS Webhook Handler -> code_commit Outbox Event
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the existing VCS webhook surface to handle push events and enqueue `code_commit` outbox events for asynchronous AST indexing.

**Motivation** — Webhook controllers must not synchronously fetch file contents or perform heavy indexing; they should enqueue lightweight events for outbox processing.

**Approach** — Extend `POST /projects/:slug/vcs-webhook` to validate push payloads (`repository`, `ref`, `commits[]`, sender) and enqueue one `code_commit` event per commit with `{ repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }`. Signature verification reuses existing `x-hub-signature-256` flow and project-scoped webhook secrets. Outbox handler performs downstream processing (including file-content resolution and index invocation).
acceptanceCriteria: VcsWebhookController extends existing POST /projects/:slug/vcs-webhook to handle push/code-intel events
Webhook payload is validated: presence of repository identifier, ref, commits[], and sender id
For each commit in the push, a code_commit outbox event is enqueued with { repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }
AstIndexService.indexCommit() is called by the code_commit outbox handler, not synchronously by the webhook controller
If event enqueue fails, the webhook logs the failure and returns a non-2xx response so the provider can retry
GitHub webhook signature verification reuses the existing x-hub-signature-256 flow; invalid signatures return 401
Webhook secret comes from the project's VCS connection record (never hard-coded)
Webhook handler is idempotent: pushing the same commitHash twice does not create duplicate outbox events (dedup by commitHash within a 5-minute window)
suggestedCriteria: Dedup is enforced with a durable dedup key (e.g. repoId:commitHash:ref) at persistence level to prevent race-condition duplicates
Push payload with zero commits returns success and enqueues no code_commit events
Missing required push fields returns 400 and enqueues nothing
If no VCS connection or webhook secret exists for project, signature validation fails with 401/404 according to existing endpoint conventions
Code_commit handler failures are retryable and observable via outbox status/attempt metadata

userStories.title: getChangeImpact API
acceptanceCriteria: GET /projects/:slug/codeintel/impact?repoId=X&commitHash=Y&changedFiles=file1,file2 returns ChangeImpactResult
impactedSymbols contains symbols whose file matches any entry in changedFiles
impactedServices contains service entities linked to impacted symbols through Symbol.file → GraphNode.sourceFile or EntityNode.sourceId matching
impactedTickets contains tickets linked to any impactedServices
impactScore is a number 0-100 computed by the formula in specification section §4
When called with a ticketId, the result includes provenance source metadata pointing to that ticket
The endpoint returns in under 5 seconds for a commit touching up to 50 files
The endpoint is gated with @RequiredPermission([KodaAction.READ, 'CodeIntel']); grants to ADMIN users, all agents, and DEVELOPER project role users
suggestedCriteria: impactScore handles sparse data by treating zero-denominator terms as zero and always returning a finite value
impactedSymbols, impactedServices, and impactedTickets are de-duplicated
Path normalization is applied so Symbol.file and GraphNode.sourceFile comparisons are stable across equivalent path formats
When commit has no indexed symbols, endpoint returns empty impactedSymbols and still computes score from available terms
When project slug is unknown, endpoint returns project-not-found in existing API exception style

userStories.title: CanonicalStateService Snapshot Read Layer
acceptanceCriteria: CanonicalStateService.getSnapshot(query) returns retrievedAt set to the server timestamp
When ticketIds are provided, tickets contains only tickets in the requested projectId
When timeWindow is provided, recentEvents contains only events in the window, ordered by createdAt DESC
activeDecisions is populated from active MemoryItem rows with kind='DECISION'
A non-existent or unauthorized projectId throws the same KodaError/Nathapp exception style used by earlier memory endpoints
The service performs canonical Prisma reads only; it does not query LanceDB, BM25, entity graph, or other derived stores
suggestedCriteria: When ticketIds is absent, tickets returns an empty array
When no active decisions exist, activeDecisions returns an empty array
Time-window filters support open-ended bounds (from-only or to-only) with deterministic ordering
recentEvents shape includes enough source metadata to distinguish TicketEvent/AgentEvent/DecisionEvent origins

analysis: Phase 4 should be delivered as a durable, incremental, project-scoped code intelligence foundation across apps/api, while explicitly addressing implementation risks surfaced in review: (1) preserve backward compatibility for RagService.importGraphify consumers by adapting DiffResult to existing writer metadata shape where needed, (2) implement robust webhook dedup with an explicit outbox dedup key instead of payload-string lookups, (3) keep parser/indexing failure isolation per file, (4) define clear LanceDB/Prisma consistency behavior and reconciliation path, and (5) treat performance thresholds as target benchmarks with measured validation, not brittle CI hard gates. The architecture remains: GraphNode/GraphLink for incremental graph persistence, Symbol table for deterministic AST index, EntityNode/EntityLink for durable operational linkage, VCS webhook -> code_commit outbox for async indexing, getChangeImpact API for deterministic impact queries, and CanonicalStateService as Phase-5-facing read layer.
